ExoVisionaries is a collaborative team passionate about technology, science, innovation and space exploration. 

Our team comprises Jannatul Nayem Esmy, our dedicated team leader with her excellent team members Priya Dev and Shaulee Bose, the passionate Researchers; Muhammad Asif, our brilliant App Developer; MD. Habibullah Galib, our visionary Solution Designer.

Through Zero To Beyond, we aim to combine creativity, engineering and interactive learning.
summary:
Zero To Beyond is an interactive, story-driven space mission design game that transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into an engaging, hands-on learning experience. It allows players to experience the journey of becoming a space mission designer by planning exploration objectives, assembling spacecraft, selecting equipment and crew, managing limited resources and preparing for lunar exploration.
Through interactive spacecraft-building environments, character-guided storytelling, engineering challenges and mission-based activities, Zero To Beyond introduces players to the scientific, technical and strategic decisions involved in real-world space exploration.
Our vision is to make space mission design accessible to students, educators, beginners and space enthusiasts by turning theoretical aerospace concepts into practical, interactive experiences.
details:
About our solution — How it works 

Zero To Beyond takes players through a connected, story-driven lunar exploration journey consisting of eight major milestones:

  1. Mission Selection: Choose a lunar exploration objective, including investigating water ice or studying lunar geology.
  2. Mission Planning: Define mission requirements and establish an exploration strategy.
  3. Spacecraft Design: Assemble and customize a spacecraft by selecting suitable hardware components.
  4. Engineering and Resource Management: Consider spacecraft mass, power, budget, fuel, equipment and mission feasibility.
  5. Crew Selection: Assign crew members and configure essential mission systems.
  6. Launch Preparation: Complete engineering checks, spacecraft packing, crew rehearsals and readiness assessments.
  7. Mission Execution: Experience launch, lunar travel, landing and surface exploration through interactive game sequences.
  8. Crew Return and Mission Debrief: Review mission outcomes, evaluate decisions and complete return-mission activities.

The experience combines interactive 2D and 3D spacecraft assembly, character-guided storytelling, educational explanations, resource-management mechanics and hands-on mini-games.

Players can experiment with different configurations, receive guidance, retry challenges and learn how engineering decisions influence the mission.

Key features and innovations 

1. Interactive 2D and 3D Spacecraft Assembly

Players can explore spacecraft components and construct a vehicle suitable for their selected mission.

2. Mission-Specific Exploration

Different lunar exploration pathways introduce scientific objectives, equipment choices and exploration activities related to water ice and lunar geology.

3. Engineering and Resource Management

Players consider engineering constraints such as mass, power, budget, fuel and equipment requirements when configuring their spacecraft.

4. Character-Guided Storytelling

Interactive characters, dialogues, hints and educational explanations guide players through the mission.

5. Hands-on Mission Activities

Players participate in spacecraft preparation, equipment packing, rover exploration, launch preparation and mission-return activities.

6. Lunar Exploration & Landing

Players experience lunar descent and surface exploration.They can control vertical and horizontal movement to approach the landing zone. Also, one can navigate landing challenges and aim for a safe touchdown.

7.Interactive Launch & Throttle Control

Players experience interactive rocket launches. They can also control throttle and thrust to manage rocket acceleration and monitor flight performance throughout the launch sequence.

8. Guided and Challenge Experiences

The game supports different levels of assistance, helping beginners understand mission concepts while encouraging more confident players to experiment independently.

9. Accessible Web-Based Platform

Zero To Beyond provides a browser-based experience designed to make space mission design accessible to a wider audience.

10.NASA Archive

 It helps to explore NASA-related mission archives, space exploration resources, and scientific information.Learn from real-world space missions and discoveries.

11. Engineering Lab

It provides experiments with rocket engineering and propulsion concepts, exploring engineering parameters and their impact on spacecraft performance.

12. Orbit and signal lab

It helps to explore orbital mechanics and spacecraft trajectories, understand orbital altitude, velocity and spacecraft movement.

13. Space Roadmap

One can choose their dream career in the space industry and receive a personalized, step-by-step roadmap with guidance on the skills, knowledge and opportunities needed to achieve your goal.

14.Cosmic Explorer

Explore the cosmos by comparing the sizes of celestial bodies, discovering travel times between destinations, and planning your own space missions.

15.Keywords and Video Link

One can find the meaning of important keywords and check more youtube video links for better understanding of the space missions

Challenges we address 

Zero To Beyond focuses on making complex aerospace engineering concepts accessible and understandable through interactive learning.

Our project addresses the following challenges:

  • Accessibility of Aerospace Education: Simplifying complex spacecraft and mission-design concepts for students and beginners.
  • Engineering Trade-offs: Demonstrating how mass, power, budget, fuel and equipment decisions affect mission planning.
  • Science and Engineering Integration: Connecting lunar exploration objectives with spacecraft hardware and scientific equipment.
  • Practical Problem-Solving: Encouraging players to experiment with spacecraft configurations, identify problems and improve their designs.
  • STEM Engagement: Making aerospace engineering more engaging through interactive environments, storytelling and game-based learning.

Our objective is to help players understand not only what a space mission does, but also why specific engineering decisions are necessary to make it possible.

Target audience and potential impact 

Target Audience:

  • School and university students interested in STEM.
  • Students interested in aerospace and space engineering.
  • Educators looking for interactive space-science learning tools.
  • Beginners interested in spacecraft design and space exploration.
  • Space enthusiasts and aspiring scientists.

Expected Impact:

Zero To Beyond aims to encourage curiosity about space exploration, improve awareness of aerospace engineering and introduce learners to systems thinking and engineering decision-making.

By providing an interactive environment for experimenting with mission configurations and resource constraints, the project can support informal STEM education and inspire future generations to explore careers in science, technology, and space engineering.

What We Would Build Next

Our vision is to expand Zero To Beyond into a more comprehensive and scientifically grounded space mission simulation platform.

Future development plans include:

  • Complete Mars Exploration Missions: Introduce spacecraft design, interplanetary travel, landing and Mars surface exploration.
  • More Mission Destinations: Add additional lunar landing sites, deep-space destinations and exploration scenarios.
  • Advanced Physics-Based Simulation: Integrate more realistic orbital mechanics, propulsion calculations, fuel consumption, landing dynamics and mission trajectory modeling.
  • Enhanced Engineering Systems: Introduce more detailed spacecraft subsystem interactions, including communication, thermal control, navigation and power management.
  • Multiplayer Collaboration: Allow players to work together as mission planners, engineers, scientists and commanders.
  • Performance Evaluation: Introduce mission scoring, engineering feedback and detailed post-mission reports to help players understand the consequences of their decisions.

Technology and Tools

1. Monorepo & Development Tooling

Built with Turborepo and pnpm workspaces, organizing the application into @exo/web, @exo/engine, @exo/data, @exo/ui, @exo/audio, and @exo/tsconfig. TypeScript 6 provides strict type checking, while Oxlint and Prettier support code quality and consistent formatting.

2. Frontend & User Interface

Developed using React 19, React Router, and Vite 8. Framer Motion supports interface animations and transitions, while Lucide React provides icons. Shared UI components handle loading progress, installation guidance, and landscape-orientation prompts.

3. 3D Rendering & Scientific Visualization

Three.js powers interactive spacecraft, lunar environments, and Solar System visualizations. The Orbit & Signal Lab uses calculated reference trajectories and line-of-sight geometry to demonstrate direct and satellite-relayed communication opportunities. Lunar reference maps present LOLA elevation and Diviner temperature data for selected study regions.

4. Simulation & Mission Logic

Custom TypeScript calculations support spacecraft mass and budget accounting, crew-consumable estimates, power budgets, delta-v calculations, and simplified ascent and transfer models. Mission logic tracks crew selection, equipment choices, milestones, and exploration progress. These are educational simulations with documented assumptions, rather than flight-certified predictions.

5. State, Audio & Offline Support

React state and reducer-based logic manage gameplay interactions, with Zustand stores supporting shared loading, orientation, audio, and installation state. The Web Audio API generates procedural sound effects, alongside recorded narration and browser-speech fallbacks. vite-plugin-pwa provides installation support and service-worker caching; offline availability depends on cached resources, while live APIs require internet access.

6. Hosting & Version Control

Hosted on Cloudflare Pages, with source code maintained using Git and GitHub. A GitHub Actions workflow is configured for production builds and deployment to Cloudflare Pages.
